comments.body:
Landed for review as Gerrit change 1950 (https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1950),
commit 82e86cbdc3 on base fcc171c16c.

EVIDENCE — the test now discriminates (AC4/AC3/AC2/AC1).

Instrumentation actually fires (this was verified, not assumed). A temporary probe printing
len(captured) inside the test reported "PROBE mcp composed = 1" and
"PROBE reconciler composed = 1" — so the recorder installed on the module global
rebar._operation_config.compose_operation_snapshot is genuinely reached by code entered
through the real MCP tool call and the real reconciler main(). This matters because
emit_shadow_snapshot resolves that name from module globals at CALL time; had it been bound
at import time the rebind would have silently no-opped and an empty capture would look
identical to a pass. The probe was removed; the "composed no operation snapshot" assertion
is the permanent guard against that failure mode.

MUT-1 — composer perturbation. Inserted into compose_operation_snapshot, immediately after
resolve_with_sources:

    sources = {
        sect: {k: ("project" if v == "env" else v) for k, v in keys.items()}
        for sect, keys in sources.items()
    }

RED: the new file fails —
  AssertionError: public Python: verify.max_ticket_description_chars source
  assert 'project' == 'env'
With the public-Python anchor line temporarily removed to show the surface blocks fail on
their own merits, the failure moves to the MCP surface's own composed snapshot:
  AssertionError: MCP: verify.max_ticket_description_chars source
  assert 'project' == 'env'

The PRE-CHANGE file (origin/main's version, copied in as a second test module) passes
5/5 GREEN under the identical perturbation. That is the direct measure of the strengthening:
same mutation, old test blind, new test RED.

GREEN: composer reverted -> 5 passed.

MUT-2 — surface perturbation. Replacing the body of _shadow in src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py
with a bare return, and separately the body of _emit_operation_shadow in
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py, each turns that surface RED by name:
  AssertionError: the MCP surface composed no operation snapshot: ...
  AssertionError: the reconciler surface composed no operation snapshot: ...
The pre-change file passes 5/5 GREEN under both. Reverted -> GREEN.

GATES (worktree venv, rebased onto fcc171c16c):
  make lint            -> pass (ruff check + format-check + config/DCO/criteria/skill/zizmor/actionlint)
  make typecheck       -> Success: no issues found in 580 source files
  python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check  -> active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0
  pytest tests/interfaces/contracts tests/unit/test_operation_snapshot.py
       tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/orchestrate                       -> 460 passed
  pytest tests/interfaces/contracts tests/unit/test_operation_snapshot.py (post-rebase) -> 268 passed

The whole-tree run is deferred to CI's Verified vote on this exact commit: this host runs the
full suite serially in ~3 hours under multi-agent contention, and detached runs here have
produced errors that do not reproduce in the foreground (nonodorous-snotty-seaurchin).

NOTE (not absorbed into this change, per scope): an earlier detached whole-tree run reported
tests/integration/test_epoch_guard_reconciliation.py failing with "Test leaked new entries
into REPO_ROOT". Root cause is environmental, not this change — tests/conftest.py's
_no_repo_root_leaks fixture snapshots REPO_ROOT per test, and concurrent `rebar edit` /
`rebar set-file-impact` calls in this same worktree wrote .tickets-tracker under that root
mid-run. The test passes 7/7 in isolation on the pristine base.

MERGED: Gerrit change 1950 patchset 2 submitted at 2026-08-20 07:09:50, landed on main as 54469ca756. Votes at submit: LLM-Review +1 (rebar review bot, PASS, no findings on PS2) and Verified +1 (rebar CI bot, https://github.com/navapbc/rebar/actions/runs/32340319547 SUCCESS), 0 unresolved comments.

PS1 carried two ADVISORY (non-blocking) LLM-Review findings, both addressed in PS2:
- _reconciler_main() left a sys.path entry behind. Kept the insert (it is the established house pattern, and popping it would strand a later import of a not-yet-loaded rebar_reconciler submodule) and documented that reasoning in the docstring.
- The empty-capture assertion message attributed the failure solely to 'no longer routes through the composer', but emit_shadow_snapshot deliberately swallows composer exceptions, so a RAISING composer produces the same empty capture. The message now names both causes — and says why the swallow is exactly what makes this external capture necessary. Re-confirmed after the reword: neutralising the MCP _shadow body still turns it RED with the new text; reverted -> 5 passed.

PS1's Verified -1 was its CI run being CANCELLED when PS2 superseded it, not a test failure.

Gates re-run on the amended, rebased tree: make lint pass, make typecheck Success (580 files), check_complexity_baseline.py --check -> active=49 new=0 increased=0 stale=0. CI's Verified +1 is the authoritative whole-tree signal on the exact landed commit.

compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

RP-04 S1 advisory review finding (change 1841 PS3). The AC1 cross-surface equivalence contract
in `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_operation_snapshot_surfaces.py` claims that CLI, public
Python, MCP, and the direct reconciler entry point all compose the same `OperationSnapshot`.
Its "MCP surface" and "reconciler surface" blocks do not drive those surfaces at all: each
re-calls `compose_operation_snapshot(repo_root=..., cli_overrides=...)` with arguments
identical to the Python block, then asserts the three results are equal. That is trivially
true, so the block stays green even if the MCP tools or the reconciler entry point stopped
routing through the shared composer — which is precisely the parity bug the contract exists to
catch.

## Approach

Drive the real entry points and assert on what they actually composed.

- MCP: build a real server with `rebar.mcp_server.build_server()` and drive a real tool call
  via `asyncio.run(server.call_tool(...))` — the pattern already used by `_call_read_tool` in
  `tests/interfaces/contracts/test_mcp_survives_non_repo_root_176d.py:26`. Use
  `explain_criterion` (`src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:245`), a pure registry read with no store,
  LLM, or network dependency, whose first action is `_shadow("mcp.read.explain_criterion")`
  at `src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:253`.
- Reconciler: call `rebar_reconciler.__main__.main()` with argv. `main` composes its snapshot
  at `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/__main__.py:570` (`_emit_operation_shadow`)
  immediately after request normalization, and `--dry-run-enumerate`
  (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/request.py:75`) returns at `__main__.py:573`, before
  any advisory lock, pass, or network effect.
- Capture: both surfaces reach the composer through
  `rebar._operation_config.emit_shadow_snapshot`, which calls the module global
  `compose_operation_snapshot` at `src/rebar/_operation_config.py:251` — a name resolved from
  module globals at CALL time, so rebinding that module attribute genuinely reaches code
  entered through the real surfaces rather than only the test module's import-time binding. A
  recorder wraps it for the duration of each surface call and returns the real composer's
  result unchanged, so the driven surface behaves exactly as in production.

Asserting instead on the surface's emitted DEBUG diagnostic was rejected: that line carries
only a 12-hex truncated fingerprint (`src/rebar/_operation_config.py` `emit_shadow_snapshot`),
which can only ever be compared against another composition, reintroducing the same vacuity.

Two properties make the contract discriminate, and both are required:

1. The recorder must have fired. An empty capture list fails with an explicit message, so a
   surface that stops routing through the composer goes RED instead of looping over nothing —
   the failure mode where a spy that never fires is indistinguishable from a passing assertion.
2. Each surface's own snapshot is anchored to ABSOLUTE expected content (repo root, envelope
   version, and two config keys with distinct provenance) in addition to being compared to the
   Python reference. Cross-surface comparison alone is vacuous: perturb the composer and every
   surface moves together, so "equal to each other" stays true while all of them are wrong.

The shared input moves off `cli_overrides` onto a project layer (`sync.push`) plus an env layer
(`REBAR_VERIFY_MAX_TICKET_DESCRIPTION_CHARS`), because MCP's `_shadow` and the reconciler's
`_emit_operation_shadow` pass no `cli_overrides`. A cli-layer-only anchor can only be asserted
on the surfaces that accept one, which is how the block ended up re-composing instead of
driving. The existing CLI block keeps its own cli-layer provenance assertion.

## Scope

`tests/interfaces/contracts/test_operation_snapshot_surfaces.py` only. No production code
changes; nothing outside this file is edited.

## Testing

The change IS the test, so its discrimination is established by mutation rather than by adding
further tests:

- Perturb `compose_operation_snapshot` to collapse `env` provenance into `project`. The MCP and
  reconciler surface assertions must go RED, and the pre-change version of the file must stay
  GREEN under the same perturbation.
- Neutralize the MCP `_shadow` body and the reconciler `_emit_operation_shadow` body,
  independently. Each surface's "composed no operation snapshot" assertion must go RED naming
  that surface.
- Revert every perturbation; the file must be GREEN.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The MCP block invokes the real MCP entry point (`build_server()` + `call_tool`) instead
      of calling the composer again. Checked by reading the file: no `compose_operation_snapshot(`
      call remains in the MCP or reconciler block.
- [x] The reconciler block invokes the real `rebar_reconciler.__main__.main()` argv entry point
      and asserts its return code is 0. Checked by reading the file and by the test passing.
- [x] Each surface block fails when its surface composes no snapshot. Checked by neutralizing
      `_shadow` and `_emit_operation_shadow` one at a time and observing a RED assertion that
      names that surface.
- [x] Perturbing the composer makes the surface assertions RED. Checked by applying the
      env-to-project provenance perturbation and observing the MCP/reconciler assertions fail,
      then reverting and observing GREEN; the pre-change file stays GREEN under the same
      perturbation.
- [x] Gates pass on the whole tree: `make lint`, `make typecheck`,
      `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reporting `new=0 increased=0 stale=0`,
      and `pytest tests --ignore=tests/external`.

compiled_state.title: Drive AC1 snapshot-equivalence contract through real MCP + reconciler entry points
